bound_proof.id_rule: validate_rpc_id before incoming_request; string ids are <=256 bytes and control-free; quote/backslash expand 2x; U+2028/U+2029 expand 3 UTF-8 bytes to 6, not worse
bound_proof.conclusion: Question text is copied at most twice as object keys and a selected preview at most once. Both are inside value_bytes(params). Submitted choices and notes are re-encoded by the same serde_json rules and are bounded by LOCAL_CONTENT before encode. Envelope, colons, brackets, and per-question map syntax fit in the 4096 reserve with thousands of bytes of slack. The check therefore rejects before publication every request whose worst-case accept reply would exceed FRAME, and it does not depend on a particular short answer.

checklist.title: Closed genuine Grok method/schema/modes; no fabricated prose/MCP questions.

checklist.title: Exact session/tool/wire RPC identity and malformed scope rejection.
checklist.evidence: grok.rs:23-26 requires a valid toolCallId. parse_form still requires exactly one of sessionId/requestId and the live session before publication. src/acp.rs:1785-1786 validates the RPC id before incoming_request, and encode echoes that same id. A grok::form or parse_form error becomes -32602 on that original id at src/acp.rs:2024-2031 without publishing an interaction.

checklist.title: Duplicate question/choice and question/option count bounds.
checklist.evidence: grok.rs:31-32 caps questions at FIELDS/2 (32) and rejects empty. grok.rs:48-50 rejects duplicate question text. grok.rs:89 and 104-107 cap each option list and reject duplicate labels. grok.rs:122-123 caps total choices, including an injected Other, at OPTIONS (256). checklist.title: Nullable flags and scalar/multiselect semantics.
checklist.evidence: grok.rs:64-76 treats a null multiSelect or multi_select as absent and therefore single-choice, rejects a non-boolean flag, and rejects both spellings together. A true flag builds an array field with minItems 1; otherwise the field is a string oneOf. The native fixture sends multiSelect null for the subsequent small question and the expected wire answer is a one-element array.

checklist.title: Original answers/previews/annotations/Other wire shape.
checklist.evidence: grok.rs:152-176 writes outcome accepted, answers keyed by the original question text to a string array, and annotations only when notes or a single-selection preview exist. Preview is copied from the offered option, not invented. Cancel is outcome cancelled. The native regression asserts the exact grok-other accept object, including Other and notes 7.

checklist.title: Shared scalar/array Other dependent-notes validation before capture and admission.
checklist.evidence: src/acp.rs:2546-2558 rejects Other, including an array containing Other, when the grok_notes_key is missing, empty, or non-string. validate_form_values is the shared pre-capture and admission validator. The reply-budget predicate does not move or duplicate that rule. The library case at src/acp.rs:3388-3416 still expects decline and missing notes to leave the responder pending.

checklist.title: Unsupported decline retains responder and is not offered natively.
checklist.evidence: grok.rs:147-149 bails on Decline. src/acp.rs:893-900 uses that result with ? before enqueue at 962 and before selection mutation at 964, so the pending responder is retained. Native decline_offered at src/tui/agent.rs:1121-1124 is false for the accept/cancel action list, and F6 at 1378-1382 returns without answer().

checklist.title: Concrete worst-case reply bound: escaping, repeated keys, previews, max values/count/RPC.
checklist.evidence: grok.rs:34-40 requires value_bytes(params) <= 489472 before schema construction. value_bytes and encode both use serde_json, so escaping is counted on the same rules as the wire. Question text is inserted at most twice as keys; a preview at most once; both are inside params. Choices and notes are bounded by LOCAL_CONTENT at src/acp.rs:2528-2529 before grok::response/encode. A 256-byte escaped RPC id is at most 514 bytes and is inside the 4096 reserve. Static compact-JSON accounting leaves at least 3726 bytes under that reserve in the minimal one-question case and more slack at 32 questions. Limit: this is static arithmetic, not an executed maximizer.
